description: Connect Calendly to list event types, generate scheduling links, and manage events.

calendly_event_canceled_trigger.description: Runs when a scheduled Calendly meeting is canceled, by you or by the person who booked it, so a workflow can follow up on a cancelled booking. It gives the meeting (name, start_time, start_display), who booked it (invitee_name, invitee_email), and who canceled it and why (canceled_by, cancel_reason).

output.answers: The invitee's answers keyed by the question's exact text, such as {"What would you like to discuss?": "Pricing"}.
output.answers_text: The invitee's booking answers, one 'Question: answer' per line.
output.cancel_reason: The reason they gave when canceling. Empty when they gave none.
output.canceled_by: The name of whoever canceled it: you, a teammate, or the invitee.
output.canceled_by_invitee: True when the person who booked it canceled, false when the host did.
output.host_name: Beta. Who hosted the meeting, such as Grace Hopper.
output.invitee_email: The email address of who had booked it.
output.invitee_first_name: The first word of invitee_name, ready for 'Hi Ada,' in an email.
output.invitee_last_name: The last word of invitee_name, for a CRM's last name field.
output.name: The event type that was canceled, such as 30 minute meeting.
output.questions_and_answers: The invitee's answers to the booking questions, as a list of question and answer pairs.
output.start_display: start_time written for a person, such as Tue, Nov 10, 2026 at 2:30 PM UTC, ready for an email or message.
output.start_time: When the meeting was to start, as machine text.
output.uri: The event's Calendly address, which identifies it.

parameters.description: Only run for meetings whose name contains this text. Leave blank for every canceled meeting.
parameters.name: event_name

calendly_invitee_no_show_trigger.description: Runs when someone is marked as a no-show for a Calendly meeting, once for each person. Calendly records a no-show only when the host marks it on the meeting (or a workflow does, with Mark an invitee as a no-show); it doesn't notice by itself that someone didn't join. Gives who it was (invitee_name, invitee_email), which meeting, and rebook_url, the link to send them to book again. On Calendly's free plan a no-show is picked up within a few minutes, for meetings that started in the last 7 days.

output.event_name: The kind of meeting they missed, such as 30 minute meeting.
output.event_uri: The meeting's Calendly address, which identifies it.
output.invitee_first_name: Their first name, ready for 'Hi Ada,' in an email with no step to split the name.
output.invitee_name: The full name of the person who didn't show up.
output.invitee_uri: The invitee's Calendly address, which identifies this person's booking.
output.rebook_url: The public booking page for the same kind of meeting, ready to send as the link to book a new time. Empty if that kind of meeting no longer exists.
output.start_display: start_time written for a person in the invitee's own time zone, such as Tue, Nov 10, 2026 at 9:30 AM EST, ready for an email or note with no date step. In UTC when their time zone isn't known.
output.start_time: When the meeting started, as machine text.
output.timezone: The invitee's time zone, such as America/New_York.

parameters.description: Only trigger for meetings whose name contains this text, such as Demo. Leave blank to match any meeting.
parameters.name: event_name

calendly_new_event_trigger.description: Runs when a new event is scheduled in Calendly. The booking is the event itself: its name, start_time, status, and who booked it (invitee_name and invitee_email), and in beta their answers to the booking questions (answers_text).

output.answers: Beta. The invitee's answers keyed by the question's exact text, such as {"What would you like to discuss?": "Pricing"}, so a step reads one answer as answers["What would you like to discuss?"] with no step to search the list. Unanswered questions are left out. Empty when the event asks no questions.
output.answers_text: Beta. The invitee's booking answers ready to read, one 'Question: answer' per line (unanswered questions left out), ready for a note or an email with no step to join them. Empty when the event asks no questions.
output.host_email: Beta. The host's email address, to message or assign the rep the meeting was booked with (a Slack message by email, a CRM owner) with no step to look them up.
output.host_name: Beta. Who hosts the meeting, such as Grace Hopper: for a round-robin or team event, the person Calendly assigned it to.
output.invitee_email: The email address of who booked it.
output.invitee_first_name: Beta. The first word of invitee_name, ready for 'Hi Ada,' in an email with no step to split the name.
output.invitee_last_name: Beta. The last word of invitee_name, for a CRM's last name field (their only name when they gave one).
output.name: The event type that was booked, such as 30 minute meeting.
output.questions_and_answers: Beta. The invitee's answers to the booking questions, as a list with one item per question, in the order the form asks them: each item has question (the question's text), answer (what the invitee wrote, blank when they skipped it) and position (its place on the form, from 0). A workflow needs no step to list the event's invitees. To read one answer by its question, use answers.
output.start_display: Beta. start_time written for a person, such as Tue, Nov 10, 2026 at 2:30 PM UTC, ready for an email or message with no date step.
output.start_time: When the meeting starts, as machine text.
output.status: The booking's status: active, or canceled.
output.uri: The event's Calendly address, which identifies it.

parameters.description: Only trigger for events whose name contains this text, ignoring capitals (demo matches Product Demo). Leave blank to match any event.
parameters.name: event_name
